- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.10) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to capture mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > -0.05) but model shows persistent downward bias, add 0.3–0.8% to forecast to reflect potential upward momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in the 20–30 day horizon when sentiment is negative; apply a +0.5–1.0% bias to forecast for this horizon.
- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.20 for 3+ days), model often lags; add 0.2–0.7% to forecast to capture early rally.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves when sentiment is mixed or mildly negative — model tends to overreact; use 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to prevent premature sell-off.
